title: An escaper that reallocates has two jobs — escape and terminate — and missing the second leaks the heap tail into the command
index_line: T-0034 · EXEC · escape routine mallocs, escapes quotes, never NUL-terminates: the shell reads the rest of the heap · c/perl/rust/go · corroborated
invariant_violated: A quoting routine is assumed to be safe because it escapes the dangerous character. But it returns a *new buffer*, and a new buffer has to be terminated — an unterminated string is not a shortened string, it is the escaped prefix followed by whatever the allocator happened to leave there, all of which the shell will parse.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated request supplies a value that a backend will embed in a single-quoted shell command
the quoting helper allocates a fresh buffer and walks the input, copying characters and expanding each quote into the escaped form
it writes the escaped bytes into the new buffer and returns it — without writing a terminator
the caller concatenates that C string into a command line, so everything after the return value to the first zero byte is included
the attacker shapes the adjacent heap (several requests, sized allocations) so the trailing bytes are their own text, and the extra quote they could not otherwise inject now appears
the shell executes the assembled command as the appliance's service account

source.http.request.value: any API field that a backend will place inside a quoted command; the API being enabled is the whole exposure

sink.exec.shell.value: the command string that receives the escaped (unterminated) buffer

guard.escaping.value: the quote-escaping helper — it is the guard, and it is what breaks: correct escaping, missing terminator

size.length.value: the allocation is sized from the input length, and the unterminated tail is read until the next zero byte, which the attacker controls by heap shaping

preconditions.expr: a quoting routine that returns a heap buffer rather than escaping in place
the return value is consumed as a C string (strcat/snprintf/system) with no length carried alongside
the path is reachable before authentication (the API is enabled and the command is built for a request that has no session)

check.spec: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://HOST/access/  # then repeat the request with no credentials

preconditions.expr: the patch for the target version touches only the quoting helper — a one-function diff is the tell

spec.method: diff the fixed build's access binary against the previous release; a single changed function around the quoting helper confirms the class

success: the command's side effect appears with no authentication and no valid session
exploitation needs more than one request (heap shaping) — a single-shot probe usually looks negative
the injected metacharacter does not have to be in the input at all; it is in the leftover heap
failure_like: the helper terminates the buffer, or carries an explicit length to the caller
the value reaches the command through argv (no shell) — then quote escaping is irrelevant
false_positive: an error mentioning the quoting function because the input was rejected — that is the guard working
a 200 from the API with no command side effect: reachability, not exploitation
assuming the single quote you sent was what escaped the context — check whether the injected byte was ever in your request

hazards: this is a guard that is *correct* at its stated job and broken at the job it also has; reviewing the escaping logic alone will pass it
one-function patch diffs on an appliance almost always mean a guard fix — start there rather than at the request parser
heap shaping makes this look flaky; failing once proves nothing. Repeat with size variations before concluding
CWE-170 (missing termination) is rarely in the CWE list a vendor publishes — they say 'command injection', which hides the real fix
non_transfers: languages with length-carrying strings where the caller cannot read past the value
shell-free invocation (argv), where an unterminated buffer cannot inject a metacharacter
helpers that escape in place without allocating

evidence.target: Progress Kemp LoadMaster GA 7.2.63.1 and earlier (CVE-2026-8037), fixed 7.2.63.2
